title: White House Spanish-Language Website and X Profile Taken Offline in 2025
description_short: White House Spanish-Language Website and X Profile Taken Offline in 2025
description_medium: Within hours of Donald Trump’s January 20, 2025 inauguration, the Spanish-language White House website was taken offline and showed a 404 error. An Associated Press report republished by PBS NewsHour also identified the White House’s Spanish-language X profile, @LaCasaBlanca, and a government reproductive-freedom page as disbanded. A White House spokesperson said the site was being edited and said the Spanish translation section would return; the report gave no restoration date.
description_long:
At about 4 p.m. Eastern on January 20, 2025, hours after Donald Trump’s inauguration, the Spanish versions of the White House website and social media accounts became unavailable, according to TrumpFile’s timeline. The Associated Press, in a report republished by PBS NewsHour, said the new administration took down the Spanish-language White House website; the site returned an “Error 404” message. The report named the White House’s Spanish-language X profile, @LaCasaBlanca, and the government page on reproductive freedom as also disbanded. It noted that Spanish pages for the Departments of Labor, Justice, and Agriculture remained available on Tuesday.

Asked about the change on the administration’s second day, principal deputy press secretary Harrison Fields said the White House was developing, editing, and tweaking its website, and that some archived content had gone dormant. He said the administration was committed to bringing the Spanish translation section back online and reloading dormant content “in a short timeline,” without specifying when. The contemporaneous reporting documents the initial outage and the administration’s stated plan; it does not establish a later restoration date or whether every affected page or account returned. The record therefore describes assets taken offline during the transition rather than a proven permanent shutdown.

supports: The timeline states that at approximately 4 p.m. Eastern, hours after Trump’s inauguration, Spanish versions of the White House website and social media accounts were removed from the internet.
The timeline says it would be updated if further context became available.
limitations: It does not explain the administration’s reason, identify the specific affected social accounts, or establish later restoration status.

supports: PBS NewsHour’s AP republication states: “Within hours of President Donald Trump’s inauguration, the new administration took down the Spanish-language version of the official White House website”; it says the site showed an “Error 404” message.

It states the Spanish White House X profile @LaCasaBlanca and the reproductive-freedom government page “also were disbanded,” while Spanish versions of the Labor, Justice, and Agriculture departments remained available Tuesday.

It quotes Harrison Fields: “We are in the process of developing, editing and tweaking the White House website”; archived content “went dormant”; and the administration was “committed to bringing back online the Spanish translation section of the website” and to reloading the content “in a short timeline.”
limitations: The contemporaneous report gives no specific restoration date and does not verify later restoration. It does not establish a quantified affected audience or downstream consequences.

rationale: Pass: the supplied timeline supports the discrete January 20, 2025 removal, and the focused source rescue resolves the exact missing contemporaneous context about the affected White House assets and the administration’s stated website-transition explanation. The staged title and short description are adequate and preserved. The frozen wording “deletes Spanish website and social media accounts” is narrowed in the long copy to the specific assets reported, avoiding a claim that all Spanish-language government accounts were removed or that the shutdown was permanent. Later restoration status remains unknown in the sources, so the proposed copy states only the contemporaneous commitment and makes no claim that restoration occurred. The previous held204 result remains recorded as HOLD/unreviewed/release_ready=false; this is a separate proposal based on the newly checked AP republication, not an approval derived from that flag.
